Source: Reuters

Posted June 29, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: Even many anti-prohibitionists do not realize how close we are to having a majority, and it is also important to understand that time is on our side. We are convincing more and more people every day, and –to put it bluntly – the generation that gives us the least support is dying off.
See
35 Percent of College Freshmen Think Marijuana Should Be Legalized Up from Seventeen Percent in 1989.
and
Column in London Times Notes Says The Change In Generations Will Change the Cannabis Laws

Moreover, as the influence of the Internet grows, our support will also grow.

In any case, it should be clear that opposing marijuana prohibition is no longer a " fringe position. " )

June 28, 2000

Should Marijuana Be Legalized?

UTICA, N.Y. (Reuters/Zogby) - No matter what it's called, weed, pot, herb or reefer - respondents in Zogby America's latest poll still say marijuana should not be legal.
(MarijuanaNews note: This article puts the best possible prohibitionist spin on the survey results, but it is quite remarkable that the American people are seeing through the media’s one-sided coverage, over 60 years of massive government lying, and the support for marijuana prohibition by most of the establishment, medical, legal, and political.

Lincoln was right. You really cannot fool all the people all the time.)

Two-thirds (65.7%) of the 1,202 adults surveyed nationwide said the government was doing the right thing by keeping the drug illegal. Almost one-third (31.1%), however, felt strongly that no harm would be done if marijuana was legalized, and 3.3% were undecided.
See
Gallup Poll Shows 73% Favor Medical Marijuana;
29% Favor Outright " Legalization "!
So What Are The Politicians Really Afraid Of?

The war on drugs has few supporters from the West, as 40.3% believe in legalization.
(MarijuanaNews note: Consider the influence of California on American culture and politics.)

In contrast, Southerners would be least likely to toke up - just 23.4% were in favor of bringing legal protection to marijuana users.

Curiously, three-quarters of couples who live together support the occasional reefer smoking (75.6%), while nearly three-quarters (71.4%) of married couples opposed legalizing marijuana.

What we asked:
" Do you think marijuana should be legalized?''
(MarijuanaNews note: Everyone knows that how a question is phrased greatly influences polling results. Obviously, they know very well that by phrasing the question this way, using the " L " word, without any qualification, they were sure of getting the highest negative response.

A number of reformers argue very cogently that we should use terms such as " regulate " rather than " legalize. " However, as this poll demonstrates, we really cannot control the vocabulary.

Nonetheless, we should insist that a truly honest survey must describe what is meant by whatever the question may be.

Of course, we are yet to hear any of the media use the " P " word – prohibition. When the media start talking about " marijuana prohibition " and not just " marijuana " we will have won a major victory.)
